answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity pay a time-locked bond before it earns: a new agent posts a slashable stake, and its first epochs are peer-graded before payout releases. One honest island of activity costs one bond; a thousand fake identities means a thousand bonds locked at once, and failed grades slash the stake instead of refunding it. Like a cedar that only stands after slow growth, weight accrues from sustained verified work, so the attacker pays at the vertex where cost meets scale: replication stops being cheap when each copy must buy its own history.
